33:37.ar: وَإِذۡ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِيٓ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ أَمۡسِكۡ عَلَيۡكَ زَوۡجَكَ وَٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ وَتُخۡفِي فِي نَفۡسِكَ مَا ٱللَّهُ مُبۡدِيهِ وَتَخۡشَى ٱلنَّاسَ وَٱللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَن تَخۡشَىٰهُۖ فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيۡدࣱ مِّنۡهَا وَطَرࣰ ا زَوَّجۡنَٰكَهَا لِكَيۡ لَا يَكُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ حَرَجࣱ فِيٓ أَزۡوَٰجِ أَدۡعِيَآئِهِمۡ إِذَا قَضَوۡاْ مِنۡهُنَّ وَطَرࣰ اۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ مَفۡعُولࣰ ا
33:37.en: And when thou saidst unto him on whom Allah hath conferred favour and thou hast conferred favour: Keep thy wife to thyself, and fear Allah. And thou didst hide in thy mind that which Allah was to bring to light, and thou didst fear mankind whereas Allah hath a better right that thou shouldst fear Him. So when Zeyd had performed that necessary formality (of divorce) from her, We gave her unto thee in marriage, so that (henceforth) there may be no sin for believers in respect of wives of their adopted sons, when the latter have performed the necessary formality (of release) from them. The commandment of Allah must be fulfilled

31:25.ar: وَلَئِن سَأَلۡتَهُم مَّنۡ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ ٱللَّهُۚ قُلِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِۚ بَلۡ أَكۡثَرُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ

Hfnwggyai9A.speaker: adnan
Hfnwggyai9A.speaker_note: Seerah Halaqah series by Dr. Adnan Rajeh; continues his own episodes
Hfnwggyai9A.title: Zayd ibn Harithah and the Rebuilding of the Kaaba (Seerah Ep 8)
Hfnwggyai9A.one_line: Zayd's choice to stay with Muhammad over his own family, making peace with the past, and the rebuilding of the Kaaba with only halal wealth.
Hfnwggyai9A.summary: He continues the years before prophethood, arguing that Allah chose a man whose upbringing and character were already ready for the message. The central story is Zayd ibn Harithah: kidnapped as a child, sold, gifted by Khadijah to Muhammad, and later found by his father, who raised a ransom. Muhammad refused money and let Zayd choose, and Zayd chose to stay. The sheikh asks what Zayd saw and answers that people remember how someone made them feel, not words; the same unnamed quality made the companions love the Prophet. From Zayd's later life he draws a lesson on the past: the day he was taken became the door to everything good, so the meaning of past events is decided by how we live now. Muslims should be at peace with the past, present in the moment and hopeful about the future, and should mature in how they face death. He then covers two final preparations: the rebuilding of the Kaaba, where Quraysh named him al-Amin and his cloak solution averted a war over the Black Stone, and the Qurayshi condition that only clean money be used. He presses the audience to check where their income comes from and urges the wealthy to help others avoid haram.

outline.heading: Opening
Why the years before prophethood matter
outline.gist: Allah chose messengers from excellent families and upbringings, so his parents, values and experiences are worth studying.

outline.heading: Khadijah's role in the story
outline.gist: Recap of the marriage to Khadijah; without her the story would have been very different, and the quality of their marriage is a model.

outline.heading: Zayd kidnapped, sold and given to Muhammad
outline.gist: Zayd was taken from his tribe as a boy, sold until Hakim ibn Hizam bought him, gave him to Khadijah, and she gave him to Muhammad.

outline.heading: A father's search and ransom
outline.gist: Harithah's grief and poetry spread across Arabia; he learned his son was in Mecca, raised a large ransom and came with Zayd's uncle.

outline.heading: Muhammad's offer: let Zayd choose
outline.gist: He refused the money and offered something better: if Zayd chose his family he would go free, but he would not send him away if he chose to stay.

outline.heading: Zayd chooses to stay
outline.gist: After an emotional reunion, Zayd chose Muhammad over his father and uncle without hesitation, saying he had seen something in him he had seen in no one else.

outline.heading: What did Zayd see?
outline.gist: Zayd kept ties with his parents for life but stayed; he never described what he saw, which frustrated the sheikh until he understood it.

outline.heading: People remember how you made them feel
outline.gist: Lectures fade and only the emotions remain; like the Sidrah covered by what covered it, some things cannot be described, and that quality is what made people love the Prophet.

outline.heading: Adoption at the Kaaba and Zayd named in the Quran
outline.gist: Muhammad declared Zayd his son before Quraysh; Zayd is the only companion named in the Quran, and the Prophet had no surviving sons.

outline.heading: The beloved of the Messenger
outline.gist: Zayd was known as the Prophet's beloved and Usamah as the beloved son of the beloved; when Zayd returned late from a mission the Prophet rushed to the door and embraced him.

outline.heading: An orphan who cared for an orphan
outline.gist: Orphaned three times himself, he cared for a child without parents so lovingly that the child chose him over his own family.

outline.heading: The worst day becomes the best day
outline.gist: The day Zayd was kidnapped led to Khadijah, the Prophet, his name in the Quran and his title; he would not trade it away.

outline.heading: You only own the present
outline.gist: The past cannot be changed; whether it was good or bad is decided by choices made now. A Muslim is at peace with the past, present in the moment and hopeful about the future.

outline.heading: Learning to deal with death
outline.gist: The Prophet's repeated losses taught him death at every level; Muslims must accept death maturely as part of life and not call past events simply best or worst.

outline.heading: Two final preparations: testimony and leadership
outline.gist: Before claiming prophethood he needed a public testimony to his integrity from the nobles and a chance to show his leadership.

outline.heading: Rebuilding the Kaaba: who dares strike first
outline.gist: After a flood damaged the Kaaba, no one dared demolish it until al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah struck; they waited a night, then rebuilt. Quraysh still believed in Allah though their worship was corrupted.

outline.heading: The Black Stone dispute nearly becomes war
outline.gist: Each tribe wanted the honour of placing the Black Stone; they dipped hands in blood ready to fight, then agreed the first to enter would judge, and Muhammad walked in.

outline.heading: Al-Amin: a testimony they could not retract
outline.gist: All the tribes accepted him as the trustworthy one, so later they could not call him a liar to his face.

outline.heading: The cloak solution
outline.gist: He placed the stone on his cloak, had every tribe lift it and placed it himself, defusing the anger and preventing a war before prophethood.

outline.heading: Only halal money for the Kaaba
outline.gist: Quraysh stipulated that only clean wealth be used, excluding theft, usury and coerced money; they knew halal from haram even before Islam.

outline.heading: Know where your income comes from
outline.gist: There is no excuse today; ask about your work and earnings, be aware of what you feed your children and do not push your spouse toward unlawful gain.

outline.heading: Halal food and accepted dua
outline.gist: Two narrations tie accepted supplication to clean food, including the dishevelled traveller whose food and clothing were haram.

outline.heading: The wealthy must make halal easier for others
outline.gist: Holding to halal matters most when money is tight; those given more must help others avoid usury, unlike those who said why feed someone Allah chose not to feed.

outline.heading: Outro

leS45QvcdpA.speaker: adnan
leS45QvcdpA.speaker_note: continues his own seerah series from last week
leS45QvcdpA.title: The People of the Ditch and the Year of the Elephant: The Last Divine Intervention (Seerah Episode 3)
leS45QvcdpA.one_line: Two stories the Prophet grew up hearing, the People of the Ditch and Abraha's elephant, read through Surahs Al-Buruj and Al-Fil.
leS45QvcdpA.summary: He continues the pre-birth context with two stories the Prophet's generation grew up on. The first is the People of the Ditch in Najran: a young man trained to serve a tyrant king found the truth, endured, and inspired a whole people to declare their faith, after which the king burned believers in a fiery trench. Reading Surah Al-Buruj closely, he argues that the condemned 'people of the ditch' are those who sat and watched, since the persecutors are addressed separately in a later verse and are still offered repentance. Doing nothing in the face of oppression is a choice. He adds a fourth group, the soldiers who obey orders, cites the obedience experiment in which most participants kept shocking a screaming man, and insists that no one carries your choices for you before Allah. A Muslim never harms another because he was told to. He then traces Amr ibn Luhay's importing of idols, Aksum's conquest of Yemen, and Abraha's march with an elephant to destroy the Kaaba, including Abd al-Muttalib asking only for his camels. Surah Al-Fil begins mid-conversation, answering the question we all ask: why does Allah allow this? Allah needs no advice and destroyed an army with birds; your job is to find your own role. This was the last time Allah intervened to change history without human effort.

outline.heading: Why pre-birth context matters
outline.gist: You cannot appreciate how much he changed the world without knowing the world he was born into.

outline.heading: Najran under the Himyarite kingdom
outline.gist: A story from decades before his birth: small Christian communities persecuted in southern Arabia.

outline.heading: A tyrant trains the brightest youth
outline.gist: The king wanted one religion for all and groomed talented boys, among them Abdullah ibn al-Thamir, as his clergy; every tyrant needs helpers.

outline.heading: The boy finds a hidden church
outline.gist: A critical thinker, he skipped his lessons, learned the true scripture from a hidden monk and became famous until the king captured him.

outline.heading: The teacher who hid out of fear
outline.gist: The monk asked not to be named because he could not bear torture, choosing seclusion over standing up, as many do and later regret.

outline.heading: Khabbab burned on his own coals
outline.gist: The Prophet told this story when Khabbab, his back burned by Quraysh, asked how long the suffering would last.

outline.heading: The Prophet's anger: earlier believers did not budge
outline.gist: He described a believer tortured brutally who never left his faith.

outline.heading: You are a hasty people
outline.gist: Victory will come, but they lacked patience; what would he say of our complaints?

outline.heading: The boy's death in Allah's name
outline.gist: Unable to kill him, the king finally shot him saying 'in the name of Allah, Lord of the boy'.

outline.heading: Najran believes, and the trench of fire
outline.gist: Inspired, the people declared faith in waves; the king dug a burning trench and threw in those who refused to renounce.

outline.heading: Oaths by the sky, the promised day and every witness
outline.gist: Our sacrifices are far smaller; Allah swears by the towering sky, the promised day and, uniquely, every witness and everything witnessed.

outline.heading: Who are the condemned people of the ditch?
outline.gist: Not the believers thrown in; the rest of the surah rules out that it means the persecutors either.

outline.heading: Sitting by the fire: the meaning of qu'ud
outline.gist: In the Quran, sitting always means failing to do what you should, as with those who stay behind.

outline.heading: The witnesses who did nothing
outline.gist: They did not dig the trench or approve it; they watched, and 'I did nothing' is exactly the charge.

outline.heading: The older sibling in the wrecked room
outline.gist: Parents punish the older child who sat by; we reject passivity at home, so why expect Allah to accept it?

outline.heading: Persecutors addressed separately, and still offered repentance
outline.gist: Those who persecuted believing men and women get their own verse, and even they had the door of repentance; so do the passive.

outline.heading: The believers rewarded; the soldiers who follow orders
outline.gist: Those who believed get gardens; the surah's mention of the armies of Pharaoh and Thamud points to a fourth group who harm because they were told to.

outline.heading: The obedience experiment
outline.gist: Volunteers told to give rising shocks kept going despite screams, and most went to the maximum because they were instructed to.

outline.heading: A Muslim never harms on command
outline.gist: We should be the few who walk out; the Prophet taught that even his command to harm should be questioned.

outline.heading: No one carries your choices for you
outline.gist: Not parents, friends or authority; you stand before Allah alone, so stop blaming others and choose carefully.

outline.heading: Helping each other, and Imam Ahmad's jailer
outline.gist: Helping one another rewards both; Ahmad told the guard who beat him on orders that he was not a helper of oppressors but one of them.

outline.heading: No blame-shifting, even under threat
outline.gist: Unless you lack sound mind, you carry what you do; you never harm someone to save yourself, nor sit and watch.

outline.heading: First lesson for his generation: stand by what you believe
outline.gist: They grew up on a story of courage and freedom of belief.

outline.heading: Second lesson: faith without strength and unity fails
outline.gist: A persecuted community dying is a moment to mourn and review ourselves, not to celebrate.

outline.heading: Five groups: be among those who resist
outline.gist: Oppressed, oppressors, their soldiers, the witnesses, and those who resist oppression; aim to be the fifth.

outline.heading: Khuza'ah and Amr ibn Luhay
outline.gist: Khuza'ah ruled Makkah for centuries before Quraysh; Amr was one of its leaders.

outline.heading: Idolatry imported from Syria
outline.gist: Amr liked the idols he saw in Syria and brought them to Arabia; the Prophet saw him in the Fire.

outline.heading: Byzantium and Aksum move on Yemen
outline.gist: Using Najran's massacre as cover, Byzantium had Christian Aksum attack the Himyarites, Persia's allies.

outline.heading: Abraha takes control
outline.gist: Ruling Yemen for Aksum, he used religion for politics and hoped to convert Arabia and rule it.

outline.heading: The great church of Sana'a
outline.gist: He built a church and invited the tribes on pilgrimage with gifts; almost none came, so he resolved to tear down the Kaaba.

outline.heading: An army with an elephant
outline.gist: Arabia had no united army; Arabs came to gawk at the elephant rather than fight as he marched to Makkah.

outline.heading: Abraha's ambitions and Abd al-Muttalib
outline.gist: Abraha wanted his own empire; the Prophet's grandfather was Makkah's undisputed leader.

outline.heading: A man who commanded respect
outline.gist: Abraha left his throne to sit with Abd al-Muttalib on the ground.

outline.heading: I am the lord of the camels
outline.gist: He asked only for his stolen camels; the House has its own Lord, then he withdrew to the mountains.

outline.heading: Birds in flocks
outline.gist: Ababil means something unfamiliar; birds are the last thing anyone fears.

outline.heading: An army wiped out; the Year of the Elephant
outline.gist: Thousands watched the whole camp die within hours; the Prophet was born that year.

outline.heading: A story he heard all his life
outline.gist: Like a father's story told fifty times, it stayed with him; Aksum later lost Yemen.

outline.heading: 'Have you not seen': a surah that starts mid-conversation
outline.gist: The rhetorical opening answers something already said, which the listener is meant to supply.

outline.heading: The question we all ask: why does Allah allow this?
outline.gist: From war to a traffic jam, we wonder why He does not intervene; the surah answers that question.

outline.heading: He needs no advice; focus on your role
outline.gist: He destroyed an army with birds and has run the universe without our counsel; ask what your part is, look inward, not upward.

outline.heading: The last divine intervention
outline.gist: Like the parting of the sea for Musa, this was the last time Allah changed history without human effort; next time the Kaaba will be destroyed.

outline.heading: Uhud: success is not owed to Muslims
outline.gist: When orders were disobeyed they lost; angels at Badr were only good news, and victory is from Allah for those who do the work.

outline.heading: Higher faith, fewer objections
outline.gist: As iman rises, trials become chances to prove yourself; he grew up on both stories and stood his ground.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: The unlawfulness of harm and protecting others
themes.note: Obeying orders never justifies harming someone, even at the cost of your life.

themes.label: Courage and commitment
themes.note: The boy of Najran and the believers stood firm while his teacher hid out of fear.

themes.label: Patience (sabr) and perseverance

Z-nBgMa1yoI.title: The First Command (Seerah Ep 9)
Z-nBgMa1yoI.one_line: The Prophet's retreats in Hira, the case for contemplation and self-honesty, the first revelation, and why the first word was 'Read'.
Z-nBgMa1yoI.summary: He covers the last preparations before prophethood. At 37 to 38 the Prophet began retreating to the mountain to think, with Khadijah's full support. Seclusion is not required of Muslims, but regular deep thought is; he cites the night the Prophet wept over the verses on reflecting on creation and sayings that one hour of reflection outweighs a year of mindless prayer. He urges each person to set aside time to ask hard questions about who they are and whether they are better than years ago, warning that those who lie to themselves end up lying before Allah. He then describes the true dreams, cautions against obsessing over dreams, lists the life lessons the Prophet had gathered, and pictures him in the cave looking at Ibrahim's corrupted house and asking what his role was. Revelation began simply, in a dark cave after six centuries of silence, with Jibril's crushing embrace, which he reads as seriousness wrapped in love. The first word, iqra, means to learn, comprehend and analyse, and stands beneath every ruling as the basis of the faith; the first five verses mention knowledge six times. He laments an ummah that does not read, then praises Khadijah's calm response when the frightened Prophet ran home to her.

outline.heading: Where the story stands
outline.gist: The life experiences before prophethood are covered; today come the last preparations before revelation.

outline.heading: Seclusion on the mountain
outline.gist: From about 37 or 38 he loved solitude and spent nights, sometimes a week, contemplating on the mountain.

outline.heading: Khadijah supports his retreats
outline.gist: She respected his need to think, carried food up a hard climb, and he met a monotheist who had contemplated in the same area.

outline.heading: Are Muslims meant to seclude themselves?
outline.gist: Retreat is not an obligation after him, but setting aside time for deep reflection on life is very positive and neglected.

outline.heading: The night the Prophet wept
outline.gist: Aisha's account of him praying and weeping all night until Bilal came for Fajr, because verses had been revealed warning those who do not reflect.

outline.heading: Signs for people of understanding
outline.gist: The verses on creation, day and night and those who remember Allah in every state and conclude He created nothing in vain.

outline.heading: Early scholars on contemplation
outline.gist: Sayings that contemplation is the light of faith and that a night or hour of reflection is better than a year of prayer.

outline.heading: Why he could no longer carry on as normal
outline.gist: We sweep the big questions aside for decades; at 38 he saw financial, social and religious corruption everywhere and needed to know his role.

outline.heading: Ask yourself the hard questions
outline.gist: Take an hour a month to ask who you are, whether you have a message and real ethics, and whether you take responsibility.

outline.heading: Self-honesty, or lying before Allah
outline.gist: Being honest with yourself saves you; those who keep lying to themselves will swear falsely before Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

outline.heading: Measure yourself against your past self
outline.gist: Compare yourself to years ago in honesty, compassion and closeness to Allah; prophethood came to him during this very practice.

outline.heading: Six months of true dreams
outline.gist: Allah eased him in with dreams that came true like daybreak; this explains the hadith that a good dream is one of forty-six parts of prophethood.

outline.heading: Do not overdo dream interpretation
outline.gist: Most dreams reflect daily struggles; take them seriously but not mystically, and ask qualified people only about recurring ones.

outline.heading: Stones and trees greet him
outline.gist: Before prophethood stones and trees greeted him as Messenger of Allah, getting him used to what was coming.

outline.heading: The school of life: his preparations
outline.gist: His wisdom came through lived experience, not mystically: loss, shepherding, trade, travel, war, peace, marriage, raising children and burying them, and contemplation.

outline.heading: Jabal an-Nur and the cave of Hira
outline.gist: Description of the climb and the view of the Kaaba and open sky from the cave, and why he chose it.

outline.heading: Looking at Ibrahim's house: what is my role?
outline.gist: Seeing the house built on Ibrahim's prayer for a safe land now full of idols, he asked what he was meant to do.

outline.heading: We have the answers he searched for
outline.gist: Humans uniquely ask about purpose; the answers he lacked sit on our shelves in the Quran.

outline.heading: A continuation of the prophets
outline.gist: Revelation continued a long line of prophets, and he would be the seal, though he did not expect prophethood since it had stayed among the Children of Israel.

outline.heading: Great ideas start in simple places
outline.gist: The final message began in a small cave, not a grand scene, because its strength lay in the idea, which reached three continents within decades.

outline.heading: A dark night at the end of the month
outline.gist: In a moonless night, after years of contemplation and hope for guidance, Jibril came without introduction.

outline.heading: Six centuries of silence end
outline.gist: The heavens had not spoken to earth since Isa; Umm Ayman later wept because revelation had stopped coming.

outline.heading: Jibril in his true form
outline.gist: He appeared filling the horizon with six hundred wings and entered deliberately to startle him.

outline.heading: Read: the threefold embrace
outline.gist: Jibril squeezed him three times, each time commanding him to read while he answered that he could not.

outline.heading: The first five verses
outline.gist: Jibril recited the opening of Al-Alaq and left.

outline.heading: Why it began with a hug
outline.gist: The embrace signalled love and compassion, but its force and pain conveyed seriousness and proved it was no dream.

outline.heading: The meaning of iqra
outline.gist: After six hundred years the first word was a command; iqra means to learn, comprehend, analyse and read situations, not only to recite text.

outline.heading: Iqra is beyond the five rulings
outline.gist: It is neither obligatory nor recommended in the usual sense; it is the foundation of the faith, an evidence-based way of moving forward done in Allah's name.

outline.heading: An ummah told to read that does not read
outline.gist: Few Muslims read books beyond school; knowledge is power, and following this first command would change the ummah quickly.

outline.heading: From a clot to growth in depth
outline.gist: Allah brought you from a clot of blood this far; keep growing in knowledge instead of stopping, rather than becoming superstitious and superficial.

outline.heading: Knowledge six times in five verses
outline.gist: Read twice, the pen, teaching twice and learning: every part of the learning process appears in the first revelation, which is no coincidence.

outline.heading: Shaking, he runs down the mountain
outline.gist: Frightened and cold after the encounter, he ran all the way down.

outline.heading: He ran to his wife
outline.gist: In crisis he wanted only Khadijah; spouses should build relationships where each is the first person the other runs to.

outline.heading: Khadijah's calm response
outline.gist: She wrapped him, listened to an impossible story and told him Allah would never disgrace him, listing his qualities, to be explained next week.

outline.heading: Outro

9:34.ar: ۞يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡأَحۡبَارِ وَٱلرُّهۡبَانِ لَيَأۡكُلُونَ أَمۡوَٰلَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡبَٰطِلِ وَيَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡنِزُونَ ٱلذَّهَبَ وَٱلۡفِضَّةَ وَلَا يُنفِقُونَهَا فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَبَشِّرۡهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
9:34.en: O ye who believe! Lo! many of the (Jewish) rabbis and the (Christian) monks devour the wealth of mankind wantonly and debar (men) from the way of Allah. They who hoard up gold and silver and spend it not in the way of Allah, unto them give tidings (O Muhammad) of a painful doom

6:151.ar: ۞قُلۡ تَعَالَوۡاْ أَتۡلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمۡ عَلَيۡكُمۡۖ أَلَّا تُشۡرِكُواْ بِهِۦ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۖ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَٰنࣰ اۖ وَلَا تَقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَوۡلَٰدَكُم مِّنۡ إِمۡلَٰقࣲ نَّحۡنُ نَرۡزُقُكُمۡ وَإِيَّاهُمۡۖ وَلَا تَقۡرَبُواْ ٱلۡفَوَٰحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنۡهَا وَمَا بَطَنَۖ وَلَا تَقۡتُلُواْ ٱلنَّفۡسَ ٱلَّتِي حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ
6:151.en: Say: Come, I will recite unto you that which your Lord hath made a sacred duty for you: That ye ascribe no thing as partner unto Him and that ye do good to parents, and that ye slay not your children because of penury - We provide for you and for them - and that ye draw not nigh to lewd things whether open or concealed. And that ye slay not the life which Allah hath made sacred, save in the course of justice. This He hath command you, in order that ye may discern

bJRQw1simLg.speaker: adnan
bJRQw1simLg.speaker_note: opens his own seerah series, saying it is his tenth time teaching it
bJRQw1simLg.title: The World Before Prophecy (Seerah Episode 1)
bJRQw1simLg.one_line: The tribal, imperial, religious and social state of the world in the sixth century, and why understanding it is the key to the seerah.
bJRQw1simLg.summary: He opens the series by arguing that the seerah should be studied repeatedly, because it gathers every Islamic discipline in one life, and that it cannot be understood without its context, just as a film's costumes tell you the era. Understanding that people functioned differently in other times also makes us less arrogant and quicker to see our own blind spots, as future generations will judge us for burning fuel. He then maps the world: the two Arab lineages, Adnani and Qahtani, who never mixed, which makes the Ansar sheltering the Muhajirun astonishing; a world population of about 206 million, which shows how large the Prophet's following really was; few inventions; medieval Europe treating filth as piety while Islam made cleanliness half of faith. He surveys the Byzantine and Sassanid empires and their Arab client kingdoms, the unruled Hijaz held together by Quraysh's control of the Kaaba, and the corruption of the age: religious exploitation, slavery, blood sports, crushing taxes, god-kings, caste, hatred between faiths and the near disappearance of tawhid. Arabia itself suffered tribal wars lasting decades over a camel or a horse, raiding as a livelihood, infanticide from poverty, riba and the oppression of women, orphans and the weak. The Prophet was sent when the world hit bottom, and the Quran's accounts of past nations are there so we avoid their mistakes.

outline.heading: Why keep studying the seerah
outline.gist: The seerah gathers every discipline, fiqh, aqidah, hadith and language, in one life and can be completed in a couple of years, again and again.

outline.heading: Context is everything: the film analogy
outline.gist: Like costumes and accents in a film, knowing the era tells you how to read what people said and did.

outline.heading: The Quran teaches through its era; we are the farthest generation
outline.gist: Without the social and political setting we miss what the Quran and the Prophet were addressing, and we are far removed from that life.

outline.heading: Life without skills, and the plight of women
outline.gist: A man who could not fight or compose poetry was useless; women's suffering makes the Quran's rulings on their rights stand out.

outline.heading: Different times, different norms
outline.gist: Grasping that people function differently across times and places makes you calmer, less racist and less arrogant, without giving up principles.

outline.heading: Judging past generations: slavery and our own cars
outline.gist: Almost everyone once accepted slavery; centuries from now people will judge us for destroying the atmosphere, yet we are not all evil, just blind in places.

outline.heading: Put yourself in other people's shoes
outline.gist: Those best able to relate to others' circumstances are the most open-minded and successful.

outline.heading: Why lineage matters
outline.gist: Family and alliance largely predicted who would follow or oppose the Prophet.

outline.heading: Two Arab lineages: Adnani and Qahtani
outline.gist: Adnanis descend from Ismail; Qahtanis trace to Eber (Hud), ancestor of Ibrahim; tribes like Aws and Khazraj are Qahtani.

outline.heading: No mixing between the two lines
outline.gist: They lived, married and fought apart; Muhajirun living in Ansari homes was mocked as unthinkable.

outline.heading: Uniting them was extraordinary
outline.gist: Pre-Islamic wars were within each line; the Prophet joining them in love and faith was beyond what people could believe.

outline.heading: Tribal protection as the only law
outline.gist: Entering a tribe without a protector could get you killed, which explains the stories of jiwar in Makkah.

outline.heading: Semitic lineage and the prophets
outline.gist: From Nuh through Shem to Ibrahim, Ismail and Ishaq, Yaqub and the Israelites, and where the Arabs fit.

outline.heading: World population: 206 million
outline.gist: Scaled to today, the 100,000 who gathered with the Prophet equal about four million, which is why the map changed within thirty years.

outline.heading: A century of few inventions
outline.gist: Backgammon, matches and toilet paper: humanity had little to offer and would have thought modern ideas insane.

outline.heading: Dark Ages for Europe, not for Muslims
outline.gist: Within two centuries the Muslim world flourished while Europe stayed dark much longer, a history we barely know.

outline.heading: Filth as piety in medieval Europe
outline.gist: Monks sought dirty bodies as a sign of detachment, cities stank, and plague swept through low-hygiene populations.

outline.heading: Cleanliness is half of faith
outline.gist: Wudu five times a day and clean clothing for prayer made Muslims visibly different in sixth-century Arabia.

outline.heading: The hanifs never died out
outline.gist: Individuals like Quss ibn Sa'idah kept Ibrahim's way and foretold a prophet from Ismail's line.

outline.heading: Byzantium and Persia: the two superpowers
outline.gist: Centuries of war between the Byzantine and Sassanid empires shaped the region around Arabia.

outline.heading: Arab client kingdoms
outline.gist: Yemen changed hands between the empires; the Ghassanids followed Byzantium, the Lakhmids followed Persia, Kindah stood roughly independent.

outline.heading: The unruled Hijaz and Quraysh's Kaaba economy
outline.gist: No empire wanted to touch the Kaaba region, which united the Arabs; Quraysh ran its summer and winter trade on that security.

outline.heading: Byzantium: religion corrupted for money and power
outline.gist: Clergy manipulated scripture to influence rulers and enrich themselves, which the Quran condemns.

outline.heading: Slavery and blood sports
outline.gist: Slavery peaked, even a lost bet could enslave you, and crowds gathered to watch men die for entertainment.

outline.heading: Crushing taxes and poverty
outline.gist: The poor were taxed heavily; poverty, slavery and ignorance left the Byzantine civilisation at its lowest.

outline.heading: Persia: rulers worshipped as gods
outline.gist: Without an Abrahamic ethic, Persian kings claimed divinity, still addressed as lord in the Prophet's time.

outline.heading: Obscene laws and social injustice in Persia
outline.gist: Laws that permitted zina and a class system that stripped the lowest of all rights, even over their children.

outline.heading: India: caste and religious corruption
outline.gist: Religious leaders at the top ranked everyone else, with severe oppression of women.

outline.heading: A prophet sent at rock bottom
outline.gist: A messenger comes when the world is failing; the Quran tells of past nations so we avoid their mistakes, not to gossip about them.

outline.heading: Hatred between faiths
outline.gist: Jews and Christians in Arabia committed atrocities against each other; tolerance did not yet exist.

outline.heading: Scripture manipulated, tawhid nearly gone
outline.gist: Both Abrahamic traditions had altered texts and practice, leaving only scattered individuals on true monotheism.

outline.heading: A catalogue of gods
outline.gist: People worshipped the sun, stars, animals and rocks, even edible idols, and later told such stories with amusement.

outline.heading: Intellect without guidance
outline.gist: Asked where their minds were, they said they had minds but no guidance; reason only goes so far without Allah's guidance.

outline.heading: The two Arab families stayed apart

outline.heading: The sa'alik: rebels against tribalism
outline.gist: Outcasts who broke from their tribes and wrote the most compelling poetry against a closed, blood-based order.

outline.heading: Al-Hutay'ah and the power of satire
outline.gist: His satire of a companion ruined a reputation until Umar threatened to silence him.

outline.heading: The War of al-Basus
outline.gist: A killed camel led to forty years of war between the cousin tribes of Bakr and Taghlib, drawing in a dozen tribes.

outline.heading: Dahis and al-Ghabra: decades of war over a horse race
outline.gist: Another cousin feud ran for about 35 years over humiliation in a race, showing a mentality that could not stop.

outline.heading: Good traits buried under garbage
outline.gist: Honesty, trustworthiness and generosity existed in that society and shaped the Prophet's upbringing.

outline.heading: 360 idols and Quraysh's sweet deal

outline.heading: No central authority
outline.gist: Each tribe's leader decided everything and heads of families spoke for them.

outline.heading: Raiding as a livelihood

outline.heading: Infanticide out of poverty
outline.gist: The Prophet named killing your child for fear it will share your food among the gravest sins; such despair is still real today.

outline.heading: Women without rights
outline.gist: Unlimited marriage, no consent, no ownership and no inheritance.

outline.heading: Riba and alcohol
outline.gist: Loan-sharking that enslaved debtors was the backbone of the economy, and alcohol had spread in Arabia.

outline.heading: Zina and oppression of orphans
outline.gist: Poverty and injustice spread zina, and the Quran repeatedly defends orphans' rights.

outline.heading: The weak had no one
outline.gist: The disabled, sick and orphaned were exploited; Khadijah praised the Prophet for standing by exactly such people.

outline.heading: Next: the good traits they carried
outline.gist: Islam came to fix the faults and keep the virtues, some of which we have since lost.

DEoUXTtxSbM.title: The Story of Salman al-Farisi (Seerah Episode 2)
DEoUXTtxSbM.one_line: Salman al-Farisi's decades-long search for the truth, and what it says about our youth, religious corruption and the truth we were simply handed.
DEoUXTtxSbM.summary: After a short recap of the Adnani and Qahtani lineages, he tells Salman al-Farisi's story in full as a window on the world before the Prophet. Salman, son of a Zoroastrian fire-keeper in Isfahan, could not accept answers that made no sense. The sheikh draws the parallel to our youth: when we cannot answer their questions sensibly we push them away, and either our deen is false or we do not understand it well, and he insists it is the latter. Young people convinced by an idea commit like no one else, which is why the early companions were mostly young. Salman escaped his father's chains, gave up wealth and status, and passed from teacher to teacher in Damascus, Iraq and Anatolia. One teacher was corrupt, which could have turned him away from religion for good; the sheikh calls religious corruption the leading reason people leave Islam. The last teacher described the coming prophet: a land of palm trees between two lava fields, accepting gifts but not charity, a seal between his shoulders. Sold into slavery on the way, Salman reached Madinah, tested each sign and embraced the Prophet. He closes with Salman's counsel to Abu al-Darda on balance and asks what we have done with a truth we never had to search for.

Recap: from Shem to Ibrahim, Ismail and Qahtan

outline.gist: Still before the birth, his story offers both religious benefit and a picture of the world at the time.

outline.heading: Born to a Zoroastrian fire-keeper in Isfahan

outline.heading: A mind that could not accept nonsense
outline.gist: Salman's curiosity would not let him accept a line of thought that made no sense, the virtue that drives the whole story.

outline.heading: Our children and the answers we give them

outline.heading: Youth commit like no one else

outline.heading: Either the deen is false or we do not understand it

outline.heading: Salman finds a hidden church
outline.gist: The priests' answers about life, creation and the prophets convinced him more than his father's.

outline.heading: Chained by his father, then escape
outline.gist: His father tied him up; he arranged with the priests to slip away with a caravan.

outline.heading: Leaving wealth, status and parents
outline.gist: A prodigy and heir walked away from everything and would not see his home for decades.

outline.heading: When youth believe, they are limitless
outline.gist: Convinced by stronger evidence, he began a journey of decades; for the young, passion follows logic.

outline.heading: Teacher to teacher: Damascus to Iraq
outline.gist: He served a pious scholar who on his deathbed sent him onward; we, by contrast, settle for half-answers out of laziness.

outline.heading: A corrupt priest exposed
outline.gist: One teacher hoarded donations; at his death Salman showed the people the hidden wealth.

outline.heading: The perfect excuse to abandon religion
outline.gist: After everything he had given up, meeting a corrupt clergyman could have made him faithless, with a strong argument.

outline.heading: Religious corruption drives people from faith
outline.gist: Distorting texts, serving oppressors or embezzling in Allah's name does more harm than media or war; one corrupt scholar can lose a generation.

outline.heading: The last of the monotheists in Anatolia
outline.gist: His final teacher knew of no one left on that way.

outline.heading: Signs of the coming prophet
outline.gist: A land of palm trees between two lava fields; he accepts gifts, refuses charity, and has the seal of prophecy between his shoulders.

outline.heading: Heading for the land of palm trees
outline.gist: He worked, bought livestock and paid an Arab caravan in Damascus to take him south.

outline.heading: Betrayed and enslaved, still faithful
outline.gist: The caravan took his fee and sold him; he did not turn his suffering into a reason to reject God.

outline.heading: Arriving in Yathrib
outline.gist: Taken to Madinah as a slave, he saw the palm groves and the two lava fields and became excited.

outline.heading: News of a prophet in Makkah
outline.gist: Overhearing his master, he nearly fell from the palm tree, was punished for his questions and waited years for the Prophet's arrival.

outline.heading: First sign: refusing charity
outline.gist: He brought dates as charity; the Prophet gave them to his companions and did not eat.

outline.heading: Second sign: accepting a gift; looking for the seal
outline.gist: The next day's gift the Prophet ate; Salman circled awkwardly to glimpse his back.

outline.heading: The seal of prophecy and an embrace
outline.gist: The Prophet showed him his back; Salman broke down, the Prophet lifted and hugged him and had him retell his story to the companions.

outline.heading: Freedom, the trench, and one of the household
outline.gist: He bought his freedom, advised the trench at al-Khandaq, and the Prophet counted him among his family.

outline.heading: Salman and Abu al-Darda: everyone has a right on you
outline.gist: Seeing Abu al-Darda's wife neglected, Salman told him his body, soul and family had rights; the Prophet said Salman spoke the truth.

outline.heading: Returning to Persia as governor
outline.gist: Under Umar he went back as governor, met people who remembered his flight, and ruled humbly.

outline.heading: What have you done with a truth you were handed?
outline.gist: Salman gave decades to find what sits on our shelves; we must not do the bare minimum with it.

GETeuchLD9Q.title: Khadijah, Waraqah and the Mentality of Iqra (Seerah Ep 10)
GETeuchLD9Q.one_line: Khadijah's testimony to his character, Waraqah's four statements, the power of sincere intention, and Al-Alaq's traits that make a person compatible with Islam.
GETeuchLD9Q.summary: He resumes as the Prophet runs home afraid. Khadijah's reply lists who he was before prophethood: he kept family ties even with those who cut him, supported the destitute, carried people who could not carry themselves, honoured guests and helped in calamities. He asks husbands whether their wives could say the same of them. Waraqah ibn Nawfal then told him he was the prophet of this nation, that the same angel came to Musa, that his people would expel him, and that he wished he could support him then. The Prophet's pained question about expulsion leads to a reflection on remembering one's roots while serving Canada. Waraqah died soon after, but his sincere intention earned him great reward, so the sheikh urges never giving up on good intentions despite Shaytan. After a pause, Jibril taught wudu and prayer, prompting a firm call to pray on time. The core of the talk reads Al-Alaq as prerequisites for Islam to work in a person: humility, compassion, openness to new ideas, objectivity and following truth wherever it leads. Without these, he argues, Muslims fall into superstition, blame jinn and treat mental illness with blown-over water instead of care. He ends with how the first surahs gave the Prophet principles, ethics, spiritual discipline and the key of Al-Fatihah.

outline.heading: Why the Meccan period speaks to us
outline.gist: The Meccan years are his favourite part of the seerah because Muslims today resemble that period more than the Madinan one.

outline.heading: Running down the mountain, unsure
outline.gist: He did not yet know what he had met, feared it was punishment, and had no ego stopping him from telling his wife he was scared.

outline.heading: Khadijah's words define him before prophethood
outline.gist: Her reasons why Allah would never disgrace him describe who he already was and what keeps a Muslim steady.

outline.heading: He kept the ties of kinship
outline.gist: He reached out to relatives who would not reach out, ended feuds even when not at fault; how can you teach children family first if you do not live it?

outline.heading: He gave to the destitute
outline.gist: Not poor himself, he used his surplus and more to support those with nothing, either giving money or helping them earn.

outline.heading: He carried those who could not carry themselves
outline.gist: Instead of scorning relatives who keep failing at life, he bore their burden; he also honoured guests.

outline.heading: Would your spouse say this about you?
outline.gist: What is the point of a life if your wife cannot honestly describe you this way; he also helped people through the calamities of life.

outline.heading: Cover me: the shock of the encounter
outline.gist: His shivering came from anxiety after meeting Jibril in his true form and being pressed three times to read.

outline.heading: Khadijah takes him to Waraqah
outline.gist: She believed in him before he did and took him to her cousin Waraqah, an old blind monotheist learned in the earlier scriptures.

outline.heading: Waraqah's first statement: you are the prophet
outline.gist: Waraqah recognised the story and told him he was the prophet of this nation, something he had not yet been told.

outline.heading: Second statement: the same angel as Musa
outline.gist: What came to him was the same spirit that came to Musa and Isa.

outline.heading: Third statement: your people will persecute you
outline.gist: Truth meets resistance at first because righteousness hurts before it heals.

outline.heading: Fourth statement: I wish I were young
outline.gist: Waraqah's statement for himself: if he lived to see the expulsion he would support him.

outline.heading: Will they really drive me out?
outline.gist: After listening politely, the Prophet only interrupted at the news that his own people would expel him.

outline.heading: Our aunt earth: remember your roots
outline.gist: Be a proud, contributing Canadian, but do not forget the lands your families came from or watch them burn.

outline.heading: A scar that never healed
outline.gist: Leaving Mecca in tears, he called it the most beloved land to him; Waraqah said none brought such a message without being opposed.

outline.heading: Waraqah asks Khadijah to stand by him
outline.gist: The Prophet left overwhelmed and Waraqah told Khadijah the road ahead was hard and she must support him.

outline.heading: A pause to process
outline.gist: Revelation paused for several days so he could absorb what he had been told.

outline.heading: Promised nothing but difficulty
outline.gist: The only promise he received was hardship in every form and exile; the early surahs asked him whether he would carry it.

outline.heading: Jibril returns and teaches wudu and prayer
outline.gist: Seated between heaven and earth, Jibril named him Messenger of Allah and taught him to purify and pray, his first lesson.

outline.heading: Pray on time without excuses
outline.gist: Only emergencies where others would be harmed justify delaying salah; never be embarrassed to ask for time to pray at school or work.

outline.heading: Waraqah's sincere intention
outline.gist: Waraqah died soon after but went on record with an honest intention to support him, earning the reward of every companion who did.

outline.heading: Never stop making good intentions
outline.gist: Waraqah is said to be raised as a nation by himself; renew your intention daily and ignore Shaytan's voice telling you that you are worthless.

outline.heading: A pattern in the first events
outline.gist: Closing Waraqah's story, he invites the audience to notice a pattern.

outline.heading: Read, the Pen and a man named Paper
outline.gist: Iqra means to learn and comprehend; the second surah was Al-Qalam and the man who confirmed his prophethood was named Waraqah, meaning paper.

outline.heading: Iqra comes before fiqh
outline.gist: Iqra falls under none of the five legal categories; it is the mentality beneath them, and any nation will prevail through knowledge, not miracles.

outline.heading: Al-Alaq: compatibility before practice
outline.gist: The rest of the surah lists traits a person must have for Islam to function in them, like a system needing a compatible motherboard.

outline.heading: First trait: arrogance and harm
outline.gist: Tughyan fuses arrogance with harming others once one feels self-sufficient; the remedy is humility and compassion.

outline.heading: Second trait: rejecting what is new
outline.gist: Quraysh forbade the Prophet's prayer because their fathers did not pray so; the remedy is open-mindedness.

outline.heading: Salman's trench: openness in practice
outline.gist: When the companions laughed at the Persian idea of a trench, the Prophet studied it and adopted it.

outline.heading: Third trait: bias and prejudice
outline.gist: Dismissing what comes from a source you dislike; you must be able to see the truth in an opponent's view and be objective.

outline.heading: Fourth trait: refusing the truth
outline.gist: Kufr versus takdhib: denying what you see is right because it does not serve you; the remedy is following the truth unconditionally.

outline.heading: Why Islam does nothing for some Muslims
outline.gist: Islam is perfect but works only in compatible people; these traits are what make learning possible, and the best in jahiliyyah became the best in Islam.

outline.heading: A way of thinking, not just reading books
outline.gist: Iqra is a mentality you can choose to adopt today by changing these traits.

outline.heading: The first five surahs and their themes
outline.gist: Each early surah represents a theme, starting with the fundamental principle of learning.

outline.heading: Against superstition and jinn blame
outline.gist: A community whose first word was iqra lives on superstition and blames jinn for marriage problems; such cultural baggage must go.

outline.heading: Mental illness in our community
outline.gist: Mental illness is becoming an epidemic in all ages; he recalls reading over water for a person with schizophrenia denied medication and therapy.

outline.heading: Quran plus real treatment
outline.gist: Recite Quran over loved ones daily, but treat the brain like any organ, as you would a broken leg; we have lost compatibility with our own deen.

outline.heading: Months without revelation
outline.gist: Revelation stopped for three to four months so he could plan; Quraysh already knew his claim long before the public call.

outline.heading: Quraysh secretly listening
outline.gist: Non-Muslims kept asking converts what new Quran had come and hid behind the wall to hear his recitation.

outline.heading: A Quran that broke the rules of poetry
outline.gist: Masters of language found the Quran ignored their rigid forms and had its own rules of recitation, and they could not get enough of it.

outline.heading: Al-Qalam as the ethical code
outline.gist: Its opening verses list traits to avoid; rule out the bad and choose freely from the good.

outline.heading: Al-Muzzammil and Al-Muddaththir
outline.gist: The first gives his spiritual needs, night prayer and Quran, needed like sleep; the second gives his mission of conduct.

outline.heading: Al-Fatihah: the key to every door
outline.gist: Everything in Islam must fit Al-Fatihah; with these tools he was left to devise his own plan.

outline.heading: Outro

2:2.ar: ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ لَا رَيۡبَۛ فِيهِۛ هُدࣰ ى لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ
2:2.en: This is the Scripture whereof there is no doubt, a guidance unto those who ward off (evil)

2:3.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
2:3.en: Who believe in the Unseen, and establish worship, and spend of that We have bestowed upon them

2:4.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبۡلِكَ وَبِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ هُمۡ يُوقِنُونَ
2:4.en: And who believe in that which is revealed unto thee (Muhammad) and that which was revealed before thee, and are certain of the Hereafter

2:5.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ عَلَىٰ هُدࣰ ى مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
2:5.en: These depend on guidance from their Lord. These are the successful

2:6.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَأَنذَرۡتَهُمۡ أَمۡ لَمۡ تُنذِرۡهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
2:6.en: As for the Disbelievers, Whether thou warn them or thou warn them not it is all one for them; they believe not

2:7.ar: خَتَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ وَعَلَىٰ سَمۡعِهِمۡۖ وَعَلَىٰٓ أَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡ غِشَٰوَةࣱۖ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
2:7.en: Allah hath sealed their hearing and their hearts, and on their eyes there is a covering. Theirs will be an awful doom

2:8.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَبِٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَمَا هُم بِمُؤۡمِنِينَ
2:8.en: And of mankind are some who say: We believe in Allah and the Last Day, when they believe not

2:9.ar: يُخَٰدِعُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَمَا يَخۡدَعُونَ إِلَّآ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَمَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
2:9.en: They think to beguile Allah and those who believe, and they beguile none save themselves; but they perceive not

2:10.ar: فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضࣱ فَزَادَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مَرَضࣰ اۖ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمُۢ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكۡذِبُونَ
2:10.en: In their hearts is a disease, and Allah increaseth their disease. A painful doom is theirs because they lie

2:11.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ لَا تُفۡسِدُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّمَا نَحۡنُ مُصۡلِحُونَ
2:11.en: And when it is said unto them: Make not mischief in the earth, they say: We are peacemakers only

2:12.ar: أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدُونَ وَلَٰكِن لَّا يَشۡعُرُونَ
2:12.en: Are not they indeed the mischief-makers? But they perceive not

2:13.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ ءَامِنُواْ كَمَآ ءَامَنَ ٱلنَّاسُ قَالُوٓاْ أَنُؤۡمِنُ كَمَآ ءَامَنَ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُۗ أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ هُمُ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ وَلَٰكِن لَّا يَعۡلَمُونَ
2:13.en: And when it is said unto them: believe as the people believe, they say: shall we believe as the foolish believe? are not they indeed the foolish? But they know not

2:14.ar: وَإِذَا لَقُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ قَالُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ شَيَٰطِينِهِمۡ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا مَعَكُمۡ إِنَّمَا نَحۡنُ مُسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
2:14.en: And when they fall in with those who believe, they say: We believe; but when they go apart to their devils they declare: Lo! we are with you; verily we did but mock

2:15.ar: ٱللَّهُ يَسۡتَهۡزِئُ بِهِمۡ وَيَمُدُّهُمۡ فِي طُغۡيَٰنِهِمۡ يَعۡمَهُونَ
2:15.en: Allah (Himself) doth mock them, leaving them to wander blindly on in their contumacy

2:16.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱشۡتَرَوُاْ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةَ بِٱلۡهُدَىٰ فَمَا رَبِحَت تِّجَٰرَتُهُمۡ وَمَا كَانُواْ مُهۡتَدِينَ
2:16.en: These are they who purchase error at the price of guidance, so their commerce doth not prosper, neither are they guided

2:17.ar: مَثَلُهُمۡ كَمَثَلِ ٱلَّذِي ٱسۡتَوۡقَدَ نَارࣰ ا فَلَمَّآ أَضَآءَتۡ مَا حَوۡلَهُۥ ذَهَبَ ٱللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمۡ وَتَرَكَهُمۡ فِي ظُلُمَٰتࣲ لَّا يُبۡصِرُونَ
2:17.en: Their likeness is as the likeness of one who kindleth fire, and when it sheddeth its light around him Allah taketh away their light and leaveth them in darkness, where they cannot see

2:18.ar: صُمُّۢ بُكۡمٌ عُمۡيࣱ فَهُمۡ لَا يَرۡجِعُونَ
2:18.en: Deaf, dumb and blind; and they return not

2:19.ar: أَوۡ كَصَيِّبࣲ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَٰتࣱ وَرَعۡدࣱ وَبَرۡقࣱ يَجۡعَلُونَ أَصَٰبِعَهُمۡ فِيٓ ءَاذَانِهِم مِّنَ ٱلصَّوَٰعِقِ حَذَرَ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۚ وَٱللَّهُ مُحِيطُۢ بِٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:19.en: Or like a rainstorm from the sky, wherein is darkness, thunder and the flash of lightning. They thrust their fingers in their ears by reason of the thunder-claps, for fear of death, Allah encompasseth the disbelievers (in His guidance, His omniscience and His omnipotence)

2:20.ar: يَكَادُ ٱلۡبَرۡقُ يَخۡطَفُ أَبۡصَٰرَهُمۡۖ كُلَّمَآ أَضَآءَ لَهُم مَّشَوۡاْ فِيهِ وَإِذَآ أَظۡلَمَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ قَامُواْۚ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَذَهَبَ بِسَمۡعِهِمۡ وَأَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
2:20.en: The lightning almost snatcheth away their sight from them. As often as it flasheth forth for them they walk therein, and when it darkeneth against them they stand still. If Allah willed, He could destroy their hearing and their sight. Lo! Allah is able to do all things

2:21.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱعۡبُدُواْ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُمۡ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
2:21.en: O mankind! worship your Lord, Who hath created you and those before you, so that ye may ward off (evil)

2:22.ar: ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِرَٰشࣰ ا وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بِنَآءࣰ وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَخۡرَجَ بِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ رِزۡقࣰ ا لَّكُمۡۖ فَلَا تَجۡعَلُواْ لِلَّهِ أَندَادࣰ ا وَأَنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:22.en: Who hath appointed the earth a resting-place for you, and the sky a canopy; and causeth water to pour down from the sky, thereby producing fruits as food for you. And do not set up rivals to Allah when ye know (better)

2:23.ar: وَإِن كُنتُمۡ فِي رَيۡبࣲ مِّمَّا نَزَّلۡنَا عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِنَا فَأۡتُواْ بِسُورَةࣲ مِّن مِّثۡلِهِۦ وَٱدۡعُواْ شُهَدَآءَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:23.en: And if ye are in doubt concerning that which We reveal unto Our slave (Muhammad), then produce a surah of the like thereof, and call your witness beside Allah if ye are truthful

2:24.ar: فَإِن لَّمۡ تَفۡعَلُواْ وَلَن تَفۡعَلُواْ فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱلنَّارَ ٱلَّتِي وَقُودُهَا ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱلۡحِجَارَةُۖ أُعِدَّتۡ لِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:24.en: And if ye do it not - and ye can never do it - then guard yourselves against the Fire prepared for disbelievers, whose fuel is of men and stones

2:25.ar: وَبَشِّرِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ أَنَّ لَهُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُۖ كُلَّمَا رُزِقُواْ مِنۡهَا مِن ثَمَرَةࣲ رِّزۡقࣰ ا قَالُواْ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي رُزِقۡنَا مِن قَبۡلُۖ وَأُتُواْ بِهِۦ مُتَشَٰبِهࣰ اۖ وَلَهُمۡ فِيهَآ أَزۡوَٰجࣱ مُّطَهَّرَةࣱۖ وَهُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
2:25.en: And give glad tidings (O Muhammad) unto those who believe and do good works; that theirs are Gardens underneath which rivers flow; as often as they are regaled with food of the fruit thereof, they say: this is what was given us aforetime; and it is given to them in resemblance. There for them are pure companions; there for ever they abide

2:26.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَسۡتَحۡيِۦٓ أَن يَضۡرِبَ مَثَلࣰ ا مَّا بَعُوضَةࣰ فَمَا فَوۡقَهَاۚ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ فَيَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡۖ وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَيَقُولُونَ مَاذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَٰذَا مَثَلࣰ اۘ يُضِلُّ بِهِۦ كَثِيرࣰ ا وَيَهۡدِي بِهِۦ كَثِيرࣰ اۚ وَمَا يُضِلُّ بِهِۦٓ إِلَّا ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
2:26.en: Lo! Allah disdaineth not to coin the similitude even of a gnat. Those who believe know that it is the truth from their Lord; but those who disbelieve say: What doth Allah wish (to teach) by such a similitude? He misleadeth many thereby, and He guideth many thereby; and He misleadeth thereby only miscreants

2:27.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَنقُضُونَ عَهۡدَ ٱللَّهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مِيثَٰقِهِۦ وَيَقۡطَعُونَ مَآ أَمَرَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦٓ أَن يُوصَلَ وَيُفۡسِدُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰسِرُونَ
2:27.en: Those who break the covenant of Allah after ratifying it, and sever that which Allah ordered to be joined, and (who) make mischief in the earth: Those are they who are the losers

2:28.ar: كَيۡفَ تَكۡفُرُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَكُنتُمۡ أَمۡوَٰتࣰ ا فَأَحۡيَٰكُمۡۖ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمۡ ثُمَّ يُحۡيِيكُمۡ ثُمَّ إِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
2:28.en: How disbelieve ye in Allah when ye were dead and He gave life to you! Then He will give you death, then life again, and then unto Him ye will return

2:29.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَسَوَّىٰهُنَّ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتࣲۚ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
2:29.en: He it is Who created for you all that is in the earth. Then turned He to the heaven, and fashioned it as seven heavens. And He is knower of all things

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

2:31.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِي بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:31.en: And He taught Adam all the names, then showed them to the angels, saying: Inform Me of the names of these, if ye are truthful

2:32.ar: قَالُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ لَا عِلۡمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمۡتَنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
2:32.en: They said: Be glorified! We have no knowledge saving that which Thou hast taught us. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Knower, the Wise

2:33.ar: قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ أَنۢبِئۡهُم بِأَسۡمَآئِهِمۡۖ فَلَمَّآ أَنۢبَأَهُم بِأَسۡمَآئِهِمۡ قَالَ أَلَمۡ أَقُل لَّكُمۡ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ غَيۡبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَأَعۡلَمُ مَا تُبۡدُونَ وَمَا كُنتُمۡ تَكۡتُمُونَ
2:33.en: He said: O Adam! Inform them of their names, and when he had informed them of their names, He said: Did I not tell you that I know the secret of the heavens and the earth? And I know that which ye disclose and which ye hide

2:34.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأٓدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:34.en: And when We said unto the angels: Prostrate yourselves before Adam, they fell prostrate, all save Iblis. He demurred through pride, and so became a disbeliever

2:35.ar: وَقُلۡنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسۡكُنۡ أَنتَ وَزَوۡجُكَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنۡهَا رَغَدًا حَيۡثُ شِئۡتُمَا وَلَا تَقۡرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:35.en: And We said: O Adam! Dwell thou and thy wife in the Garden, and eat ye freely (of the fruits) thereof where ye will; but come not nigh this tree lest ye become wrong-doers

2:36.ar: فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ عَنۡهَا فَأَخۡرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِۖ وَقُلۡنَا ٱهۡبِطُواْ بَعۡضُكُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ عَدُوࣱّۖ وَلَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مُسۡتَقَرࣱّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينࣲ‏
2:36.en: But Satan caused them to deflect therefrom and expelled them from the (happy) state in which they were; and We said: Fall down, one of you a foe unto the other! There shall be for you on earth a habitation and provision for a time

2:37.ar: فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتࣲ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:37.en: Then Adam received from his Lord words (of revelation), and He relented toward him. Lo! He is the relenting, the Merciful

2:38.ar: قُلۡنَا ٱهۡبِطُواْ مِنۡهَا جَمِيعࣰ اۖ فَإِمَّا يَأۡتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّي هُدࣰ ى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَايَ فَلَا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ
2:38.en: We said: Go down, all of you, from hence; but verily there cometh unto you from Me a guidance; and whoso followeth My guidance, there shall no fear come upon them neither shall they grieve

2:39.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَكَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
2:39.en: But they who disbelieve, and deny Our revelations, such are rightful Peoples of the Fire. They will abide therein

2:40.ar: يَٰبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَتِيَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنۡعَمۡتُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَأَوۡفُواْ بِعَهۡدِيٓ أُوفِ بِعَهۡدِكُمۡ وَإِيَّٰيَ فَٱرۡهَبُونِ
2:40.en: O Children of Israel! Remember My favour wherewith I favoured you, and fulfil your (part of the) covenant, I shall fulfil My (part of the) covenant, and fear Me

2:41.ar: وَءَامِنُواْ بِمَآ أَنزَلۡتُ مُصَدِّقࣰ ا لِّمَا مَعَكُمۡ وَلَا تَكُونُوٓاْ أَوَّلَ كَافِرِۭ بِهِۦۖ وَلَا تَشۡتَرُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِي ثَمَنࣰ ا قَلِيلࣰ ا وَإِيَّٰيَ فَٱتَّقُونِ
2:41.en: And believe in that which I reveal, confirming that which ye possess already (of the Scripture), and be not first to disbelieve therein, and part not with My revelations for a trifling price, and keep your duty unto Me

2:42.ar: وَلَا تَلۡبِسُواْ ٱلۡحَقَّ بِٱلۡبَٰطِلِ وَتَكۡتُمُواْ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَأَنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:42.en: Confound not truth with falsehood, nor knowingly conceal the truth

2:43.ar: وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱرۡكَعُواْ مَعَ ٱلرَّٰكِعِينَ
2:43.en: Establish worship, pay the poor-due, and bow your heads with those who bow (in worship)

2:44.ar: ۞أَتَأۡمُرُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ بِٱلۡبِرِّ وَتَنسَوۡنَ أَنفُسَكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ تَتۡلُونَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ
2:44.en: Enjoin ye righteousness upon mankind while ye yourselves forget (to practise it)? And ye are readers of the Scripture! Have ye then no sense

2:45.ar: وَٱسۡتَعِينُواْ بِٱلصَّبۡرِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِۚ وَإِنَّهَا لَكَبِيرَةٌ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلۡخَٰشِعِينَ
2:45.en: Seek help in patience and prayer; and truly it is hard save for the humble-minded

2:46.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلَٰقُواْ رَبِّهِمۡ وَأَنَّهُمۡ إِلَيۡهِ رَٰجِعُونَ
2:46.en: Who know that they will have to meet their Lord, and that unto Him they are returning

2:47.ar: يَٰبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَتِيَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنۡعَمۡتُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَأَنِّي فَضَّلۡتُكُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
2:47.en: O Children of Israel! Remember My favour wherewith I favoured you and how I preferred you to (all) creatures

2:48.ar: وَٱتَّقُواْ يَوۡمࣰ ا لَّا تَجۡزِي نَفۡسٌ عَن نَّفۡسࣲ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يُقۡبَلُ مِنۡهَا شَفَٰعَةࣱ وَلَا يُؤۡخَذُ مِنۡهَا عَدۡلࣱ وَلَا هُمۡ يُنصَرُونَ
2:48.en: And guard yourselves against a day when no soul will in aught avail another, nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will compensation be received from it, nor will they be helped

2:49.ar: وَإِذۡ نَجَّيۡنَٰكُم مِّنۡ ءَالِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ يَسُومُونَكُمۡ سُوٓءَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ يُذَبِّحُونَ أَبۡنَآءَكُمۡ وَيَسۡتَحۡيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمۡۚ وَفِي ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ عَظِيمࣱ‏
2:49.en: And (remember) when We did deliver you from Pharaoh's folk, who were afflicting you with dreadful torment, slaying your sons and sparing your women: that was a tremendous trial from your Lord

2:50.ar: وَإِذۡ فَرَقۡنَا بِكُمُ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ فَأَنجَيۡنَٰكُمۡ وَأَغۡرَقۡنَآ ءَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَأَنتُمۡ تَنظُرُونَ
2:50.en: And when We brought you through the sea and rescued you, and drowned the folk of Pharaoh in your sight

2:51.ar: وَإِذۡ وَٰعَدۡنَا مُوسَىٰٓ أَرۡبَعِينَ لَيۡلَةࣰ ثُمَّ ٱتَّخَذۡتُمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ وَأَنتُمۡ ظَٰلِمُونَ
2:51.en: And when We did appoint for Moses forty nights (of solitude), and then ye chose the calf, when he had gone from you, and were wrong-doers

2:52.ar: ثُمَّ عَفَوۡنَا عَنكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:52.en: Then, even after that, We pardoned you in order that ye might give thanks

2:53.ar: وَإِذۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا مُوسَى ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡفُرۡقَانَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَهۡتَدُونَ
2:53.en: And when We gave unto Moses the Scripture and the criterion (of right and wrong), that ye might be led aright

2:54.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦ يَٰقَوۡمِ إِنَّكُمۡ ظَلَمۡتُمۡ أَنفُسَكُم بِٱتِّخَاذِكُمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ فَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ بَارِئِكُمۡ فَٱقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ عِندَ بَارِئِكُمۡ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡكُمۡۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:54.en: And when Moses said unto his people: O my people! Ye have wronged yourselves by your choosing of the calf (for worship) so turn in penitence to your Creator, and kill (the guilty) yourselves. That will be best for you with your Creator and He will relent toward you. Lo! He is the Relenting, the Merciful

2:55.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡتُمۡ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى ٱللَّهَ جَهۡرَةࣰ فَأَخَذَتۡكُمُ ٱلصَّٰعِقَةُ وَأَنتُمۡ تَنظُرُونَ
2:55.en: And when ye said: O Moses! We will not believe in thee till we see Allah plainly; and even while ye gazed the lightning seized you

2:56.ar: ثُمَّ بَعَثۡنَٰكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَوۡتِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:56.en: Then We revived you after your extinction, that ye might give thanks

2:57.ar: وَظَلَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡغَمَامَ وَأَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلۡوَىٰۖ كُلُواْ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقۡنَٰكُمۡۚ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَظۡلِمُونَ
2:57.en: And We caused the white cloud to overshadow you and sent down on you the manna and the quails, (saying): Eat of the good things wherewith We have provided you - they wronged Us not, but they did wrong themselves

2:58.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا ٱدۡخُلُواْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةَ فَكُلُواْ مِنۡهَا حَيۡثُ شِئۡتُمۡ رَغَدࣰ ا وَٱدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡبَابَ سُجَّدࣰ ا وَقُولُواْ حِطَّةࣱ نَّغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ خَطَٰيَٰكُمۡۚ وَسَنَزِيدُ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
2:58.en: And when We said: Go into this township and eat freely of that which is therein, and enter the gate prostrate, and say: "Repentance." We will forgive you your sins and will increase (reward) for the right-doers

2:59.ar: فَبَدَّلَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ قَوۡلًا غَيۡرَ ٱلَّذِي قِيلَ لَهُمۡ فَأَنزَلۡنَا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ رِجۡزࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفۡسُقُونَ
2:59.en: But those who did wrong changed the word which had been told them for another saying, and We sent down upon the evil-doers wrath from heaven for their evil-doing

2:60.ar: ۞وَإِذِ ٱسۡتَسۡقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦ فَقُلۡنَا ٱضۡرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلۡحَجَرَۖ فَٱنفَجَرَتۡ مِنۡهُ ٱثۡنَتَا عَشۡرَةَ عَيۡنࣰ اۖ قَدۡ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسࣲ مَّشۡرَبَهُمۡۖ كُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ مِن رِّزۡقِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا تَعۡثَوۡاْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مُفۡسِدِينَ
2:60.en: And when Moses asked for water for his people, We said: Smite with thy staff the rock. And there gushed out therefrom twelve springs (so that) each tribe knew their drinking-place. Eat and drink of that which Allah hath provided, and do not act corruptly, making mischief in the earth

2:61.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡتُمۡ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصۡبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامࣲ وَٰحِدࣲ فَٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخۡرِجۡ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ مِنۢ بَقۡلِهَا وَقِثَّآئِهَا وَفُومِهَا وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَاۖ قَالَ أَتَسۡتَبۡدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِي هُوَ أَدۡنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِي هُوَ خَيۡرٌۚ ٱهۡبِطُواْ مِصۡرࣰ ا فَإِنَّ لَكُم مَّا سَأَلۡتُمۡۗ وَضُرِبَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ وَٱلۡمَسۡكَنَةُ وَبَآءُو بِغَضَبࣲ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ يَكۡفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَواْ وَّكَانُواْ يَعۡتَدُونَ
2:61.en: And when ye said: O Moses! We are weary of one kind of food; so call upon thy Lord for us that He bring forth for us of that which the earth groweth - of its herbs and its cucumbers and its corn and its lentils and its onions. He said: Would ye exchange that which is higher for that which is lower? Go down to settled country, thus ye shall get that which ye demand. And humiliation and wretchedness were stamped upon them and they were visited with wrath from Allah. That was because they disbelieved in Allah's revelations and slew the prophets wrongfully. That was for their disobedience and transgression

2:281.ar: وَٱتَّقُواْ يَوۡمࣰ ا تُرۡجَعُونَ فِيهِ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ ثُمَّ تُوَفَّىٰ كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ مَّا كَسَبَتۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ
2:281.en: And guard yourselves against a day in which ye will be brought back to Allah. Then every soul will be paid in full that which it hath earned, and they will not be wronged

2:62.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ وَٱلصَّٰبِـِٔينَ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَلَهُمۡ أَجۡرُهُمۡ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ وَلَا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ
2:62.en: Lo! Those who believe (in that which is revealed unto thee, Muhammad), and those who are Jews, and Christians, and Sabaeans - whoever believeth in Allah and the Last Day and doeth right - surely their reward is with their Lord, and there shall no fear come upon them neither shall they grieve

2:63.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِيثَٰقَكُمۡ وَرَفَعۡنَا فَوۡقَكُمُ ٱلطُّورَ خُذُواْ مَآ ءَاتَيۡنَٰكُم بِقُوَّةࣲ وَٱذۡكُرُواْ مَا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
2:63.en: And (remember, O Children of Israel) when We made a covenant with you and caused the mount to tower above you, (saying): Hold fast that which We have given you, and remember that which is therein, that ye may ward off (evil)

2:64.ar: ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيۡتُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَۖ فَلَوۡلَا فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَرَحۡمَتُهُۥ لَكُنتُم مِّنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
2:64.en: Then, even after that, ye turned away, and if it had not been for the grace of Allah and His mercy ye had been among the losers

2:65.ar: وَلَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱعۡتَدَوۡاْ مِنكُمۡ فِي ٱلسَّبۡتِ فَقُلۡنَا لَهُمۡ كُونُواْ قِرَدَةً خَٰسِـِٔينَ
2:65.en: And ye know of those of you who broke the Sabbath, how We said unto them: Be ye apes, despised and hated

2:66.ar: فَجَعَلۡنَٰهَا نَكَٰلࣰ ا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهَا وَمَا خَلۡفَهَا وَمَوۡعِظَةࣰ لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ
2:66.en: And We made it an example to their own and to succeeding generations, and an admonition to the Allah-fearing

2:67.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡمُرُكُمۡ أَن تَذۡبَحُواْ بَقَرَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَتَّخِذُنَا هُزُوࣰ اۖ قَالَ أَعُوذُ بِٱللَّهِ أَنۡ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
2:67.en: And when Moses said unto his people: Lo! Allah commandeth you that ye sacrifice a cow, they said: Dost thou make game of us? He answered: Allah forbid that I should be among the foolish

2:68.ar: قَالُواْ ٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةࣱ لَّا فَارِضࣱ وَلَا بِكۡرٌ عَوَانُۢ بَيۡنَ ذَٰلِكَۖ فَٱفۡعَلُواْ مَا تُؤۡمَرُونَ
2:68.en: They said: Pray for us unto thy Lord that He make clear to us what (cow) she is. (Moses) answered: Lo! He saith, Verily she is a cow neither with calf nor immature; (she is) between the two conditions; so do that which ye are commanded

2:69.ar: قَالُواْ ٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا لَوۡنُهَاۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةࣱ صَفۡرَآءُ فَاقِعࣱ لَّوۡنُهَا تَسُرُّ ٱلنَّٰظِرِينَ
2:69.en: They said: Pray for us unto thy Lord that He make clear to us of what colour she is. (Moses) answered: Lo! He saith: Verily she is a yellow cow. Bright is her colour, gladdening beholders

2:70.ar: قَالُواْ ٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَ إِنَّ ٱلۡبَقَرَ تَشَٰبَهَ عَلَيۡنَا وَإِنَّآ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَمُهۡتَدُونَ
2:70.en: They said: Pray for us unto thy Lord that He make clear to us what (cow) she is. Lo! cows are much alike to us; and Lo! if Allah wills, we may be led aright

2:71.ar: قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةࣱ لَّا ذَلُولࣱ تُثِيرُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَلَا تَسۡقِي ٱلۡحَرۡثَ مُسَلَّمَةࣱ لَّا شِيَةَ فِيهَاۚ قَالُواْ ٱلۡـَٰٔنَ جِئۡتَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ فَذَبَحُوهَا وَمَا كَادُواْ يَفۡعَلُونَ
2:71.en: (Moses) answered: Lo! He saith: Verily she is a cow unyoked; she plougheth not the soil nor watereth the tilth; whole and without mark. They said: Now thou bringest the truth. So they sacrificed her, though almost they did not

2:72.ar: وَإِذۡ قَتَلۡتُمۡ نَفۡسࣰ ا فَٱدَّٰرَٰٔتُمۡ فِيهَاۖ وَٱللَّهُ مُخۡرِجࣱ مَّا كُنتُمۡ تَكۡتُمُونَ
2:72.en: And (remember) when ye slew a man and disagreed concerning it and Allah brought forth that which ye were hiding

2:73.ar: فَقُلۡنَا ٱضۡرِبُوهُ بِبَعۡضِهَاۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُحۡيِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ وَيُرِيكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ
2:73.en: And We said: Smite him with some of it. Thus Allah bringeth the dead to life and showeth you His portents so that ye may understand

2:74.ar: ثُمَّ قَسَتۡ قُلُوبُكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِيَ كَٱلۡحِجَارَةِ أَوۡ أَشَدُّ قَسۡوَةࣰۚ وَإِنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنۡهُ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُۚ وَإِنَّ مِنۡهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ فَيَخۡرُجُ مِنۡهُ ٱلۡمَآءُۚ وَإِنَّ مِنۡهَا لَمَا يَهۡبِطُ مِنۡ خَشۡيَةِ ٱللَّهِۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
2:74.en: Then, even after that, your hearts were hardened and became as rocks, or worse than rocks, for hardness. For indeed there are rocks from out which rivers gush, and indeed there are rocks which split asunder so that water floweth from them. And indeed there are rocks which fall down for the fear of Allah. Allah is not unaware of what ye do

2:75.ar: ۞أَفَتَطۡمَعُونَ أَن يُؤۡمِنُواْ لَكُمۡ وَقَدۡ كَانَ فَرِيقࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ يَسۡمَعُونَ كَلَٰمَ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُحَرِّفُونَهُۥ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا عَقَلُوهُ وَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ
2:75.en: Have ye any hope that they will be true to you when a party of them used to listen to the word of Allah, then used to change it, after they had understood it, knowingly

2:76.ar: وَإِذَا لَقُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ قَالُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَا بَعۡضُهُمۡ إِلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ قَالُوٓاْ أَتُحَدِّثُونَهُم بِمَا فَتَحَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ لِيُحَآجُّوكُم بِهِۦ عِندَ رَبِّكُمۡۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ
2:76.en: And when they fall in with those who believe, they say: We believe. But when they go apart one with another they say: Prate ye to them of that which Allah hath disclosed to you that they may contend with you before your Lord concerning it? Have ye then no sense

2:77.ar: أَوَلَا يَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعۡلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعۡلِنُونَ
2:77.en: Are they then unaware that Allah knoweth that which they keep hidden and that which they proclaim

2:78.ar: وَمِنۡهُمۡ أُمِّيُّونَ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ إِلَّآ أَمَانِيَّ وَإِنۡ هُمۡ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ
2:78.en: Among them are unlettered folk who know the Scripture not except from hearsay. They but guess

2:79.ar: فَوَيۡلࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ يَكۡتُبُونَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِأَيۡدِيهِمۡ ثُمَّ يَقُولُونَ هَٰذَا مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ لِيَشۡتَرُواْ بِهِۦ ثَمَنࣰ ا قَلِيلࣰ اۖ فَوَيۡلࣱ لَّهُم مِّمَّا كَتَبَتۡ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَوَيۡلࣱ لَّهُم مِّمَّا يَكۡسِبُونَ
2:79.en: Therefore woe be unto those who write the Scripture with their hands and then say, "This is from Allah," that they may purchase a small gain therewith. Woe unto them for that their hands have written, and woe unto them for that they earn thereby

2:80.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَن تَمَسَّنَا ٱلنَّارُ إِلَّآ أَيَّامࣰ ا مَّعۡدُودَةࣰۚ قُلۡ أَتَّخَذۡتُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ عَهۡدࣰ ا فَلَن يُخۡلِفَ ٱللَّهُ عَهۡدَهُۥٓۖ أَمۡ تَقُولُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:80.en: And they say: The Fire (of punishment) will not touch us save for a certain number of days. Say: Have ye received a covenant from Allah - truly Allah will not break His covenant - or tell ye concerning Allah that which ye know not

2:81.ar: بَلَىٰۚ مَن كَسَبَ سَيِّئَةࣰ وَأَحَٰطَتۡ بِهِۦ خَطِيٓـَٔتُهُۥ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
2:81.en: Nay, but whosoever hath done evil and his sin surroundeth him; such are rightful owners of the Fire; they will abide therein

2:82.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلۡجَنَّةِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
2:82.en: And those who believe and do good works: such are rightful owners of the Garden. They will abide therein

2:83.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِيثَٰقَ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ لَا تَعۡبُدُونَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَانࣰ ا وَذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينِ وَقُولُواْ لِلنَّاسِ حُسۡنࣰ ا وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيۡتُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا مِّنكُمۡ وَأَنتُم مُّعۡرِضُونَ
2:83.en: And (remember) when We made a covenant with the Children of Israel, (saying): Worship none save Allah (only), and be good to parents and to kindred and to orphans and the needy, and speak kindly to mankind; and establish worship and pay the poor-due. Then, after that, ye slid back, save a few of you, being averse

2:84.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِيثَٰقَكُمۡ لَا تَسۡفِكُونَ دِمَآءَكُمۡ وَلَا تُخۡرِجُونَ أَنفُسَكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِكُمۡ ثُمَّ أَقۡرَرۡتُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ تَشۡهَدُونَ
